payload.prompt: International rinks are usually wider than NHL rinks.

scene.alt: Rink comparison showing wider international ice.

explanation.correct: True. The international standard is about 98 feet (30 meters) wide, while the NHL's rink is 85 feet. Some big events borrow NHL-size ice, so check the venue. More width means more room to skate and pass.
explanation.incorrect: International rinks are usually wider: roughly 98 feet against the NHL's 85. The extra space changes how players use the ice.

payload.prompt: Which is a common difference between international and NHL hockey?

options.text: International rinks are usually wider.
International games are two 30-minute halves.
International games have no penalty box.
International hockey uses a bigger puck.

explanation.correct: Right. The wider ice is the most visible difference. International games are still three 20-minute periods with penalties and the same puck.
explanation.incorrect: International hockey still has three 20-minute periods, a penalty box and the same puck. The big visible difference is usually the wider rink.

statement.speaker: Riley
statement.text: Nobody drops the gloves at the Olympics. They'd be tossed out.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: Fighting is punished in international hockey, not tolerated.
options.explanation: Right. Under international rules a fight draws a serious penalty, which is why you almost never see one at the Olympics.

options.text: Players are not allowed to touch each other at all.
options.explanation: Checking and physical play are part of international hockey. Only fighting is the problem.

options.text: The Olympics have no penalties.
options.explanation: International hockey has penalties and power plays like any other hockey.

payload.translation: In international hockey, fighting is a punishable offense, so players do not do it. It is one reason the style feels different from the NHL.

followUps.line: Does the no-fighting rule change how the games feel?
followUps.why: Invites her take on the style of play.

followUps.line: Is that also how the PWHL treats fighting?
followUps.why: Connects international hockey to the PWHL branch.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: You do not need the exact penalty. 'They get ejected' is enough.

payload.template: International rinks are typically about {{intl}} feet wide, while the NHL's rink is {{nhl}} feet wide.

explanation.correct: Right. International ice is about 98 feet wide (30 meters) and the NHL's is 85 feet. That 13-foot gap is a lot of extra room.
explanation.incorrect: International rinks are about 98 feet wide and the NHL's is 85 feet. The wider ice gives players more room to skate and pass.

payload.prompt: Every international tournament uses exactly the NHL's overtime format.

scene.alt: Overtime play in an international tournament.

explanation.correct: False. Each tournament sets its own overtime and shootout rules, and medal games can be different from early rounds. Do not assume the NHL format.
explanation.incorrect: Overtime depends on the tournament and the round. Medal games in particular can play out differently from an NHL game.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: The 2026 Olympic gold medal games both went to overtime.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: The men's and women's finals were both decided in overtime.
options.explanation: Right. The U.S. beat Canada in overtime in both the women's and men's gold medal games in 2026.

options.text: Only the men's final went to overtime.
options.explanation: Both finals went to overtime. That is what made the 2026 tournament so memorable.

options.text: The Olympics have only one gold medal game.
options.explanation: There are separate men's and women's tournaments, each with its own gold medal game.

payload.translation: At the 2026 Olympics, both gold medal games, women's and men's, went to overtime. The U.S. won both against Canada.

followUps.line: Which of the two games was harder to watch?
followUps.why: Shows you know there were two finals and invites her reaction.

followUps.line: Where were you when it ended?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you only caught highlights, say so. Fans love sharing the full story.

payload.prompt: How does an Olympic hockey tournament generally work?

options.text: Every team plays every other team once, and the top two meet for gold.
Teams play round-robin games in groups, then a knockout round decides the medals.
It is a single-elimination bracket from the first game.
Only the ten best teams in the world are allowed to play.

explanation.correct: Right. Group games come first and then the knockout rounds decide who reaches the medal games. Exact group sizes change from one Olympics to the next.
explanation.incorrect: Olympic hockey starts with group round-robin games and then moves to knockout rounds. It is not one big round-robin or a pure bracket.

statement.speaker: Alex
statement.text: It was amazing having the NHL's stars back at the Olympics in 2026.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: NHL players took part in the Olympics again, so the men's tournament had the world's top talent.
options.explanation: Right. NHL players were back at the Olympics in 2026 after missing 2018 and 2022, so the men's tournament was best-on-best again.

options.text: The Olympics replaced the NHL season.
options.explanation: The NHL paused its season for the Games. It did not replace it.

options.text: Only young prospects played in the tournament.
options.explanation: The rosters were full of established stars, which is why fans were so excited.

payload.translation: NHL players returned to the Olympics in 2026, which made the men's tournament a true best-on-best event.

followUps.line: Who was your favorite to watch?
followUps.why: Invites her to share a personal highlight.

followUps.line: Did it feel different than other years?
followUps.why: Shows you know the NHL had missed a few Olympics.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Saying 'the NHL guys were back' is a perfectly good fan summary.

payload.prompt: How many hockey medals are awarded at each Olympics?

options.text: Two: one gold each for men and women.
Four: gold and silver for men and for women.
Six: gold, silver and bronze for men and for women.
Twelve: medals for every team in both tournaments.

explanation.correct: Right. Both the men's and women's tournaments award gold, silver and bronze, so there are six hockey medals in total.
explanation.incorrect: Each tournament awards three medals: gold, silver and bronze. With a men's and a women's tournament, that makes six.

payload.prompt: Match each Olympic rivalry to its story.

pairs.definition: North American neighbors who met in both gold medal games in 2026.
The Cold War showdown behind the 1980 Miracle on Ice.
Nordic neighbors that have met in many big tournament games.

explanation.summary: Olympic rivalries mix hockey with history, geography and national pride. That is why the games feel bigger than the standings.
explanation.sayThisLine: USA and Canada, twice in one Olympics. Wow.

payload.prompt: What separates the World Championship from the World Juniors?

options.text: The Worlds is yearly and the Juniors is every four years.
The Worlds is for senior players and the Juniors is for players under 20.
The Worlds is held in Europe and the Juniors in North America.
Only the Juniors hands out medals.

explanation.correct: Right. The Worlds is the senior national-team championship, held each spring. The World Juniors is for players under 20, and many future NHL stars show up there first.
explanation.incorrect: Both are yearly and both award medals. The difference is age: senior players at the Worlds, under-20 players at the Juniors.

payload.template: The World Juniors are held every {{season}} and are a {{description}} for young players. The Worlds feature {{players}}.

explanation.correct: Right. The Juniors run every year around the holidays, and the Worlds is the senior championship in the spring. Some NHL stars cannot join because their own playoffs are still on.
explanation.incorrect: Both tournaments are annual. The Juniors run around Christmas and New Year, and the Worlds brings senior national teams together in the spring.

payload.prompt: Why does a big World Juniors matter for a young player?

options.text: It guarantees a spot on an NHL team.
It lets scouts and fans see him perform under pressure against the best players his age.
It is the only competition young players enter.
Players who win it never reach the NHL.

explanation.correct: Right. The Juniors is a high-pressure showcase. A great tournament raises a player's profile, though it guarantees nothing.
explanation.incorrect: The Juniors puts young stars on a big stage, but it does not guarantee an NHL job, and it is not the only tournament for young players.

statement.speaker: Jordan
statement.text: The World Juniors are basically a holiday tradition for hockey fans.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: The tournament runs each year around Christmas and New Year, and fans look forward to it.
options.explanation: Right. The World Juniors typically run from late December into early January.

options.text: The tournament happens once and never again.
options.explanation: It is an annual event and fans build their holidays around it.

options.text: Only families watch it.
options.explanation: Fans of all kinds watch, including scouts and hockey nerds.

payload.translation: The World Juniors is an annual tournament over the holidays that many fans treat as a tradition.

followUps.line: Which team do you root for at the Juniors?
followUps.why: Invites her to share her loyalty.

followUps.line: Who is a player to watch this year?
followUps.why: Gets her sharing prospects she loves.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Saying 'it is a Christmas thing for hockey fans' is an honest summary.

payload.prompt: The World Juniors is open to players of any age.

scene.alt: A roster sheet showing birth years for the World Juniors.

explanation.correct: False. The World Juniors is an under-20 tournament. That age limit is what makes it a showcase for rising stars.
explanation.incorrect: The Juniors is limited to players under 20. Open-age tournaments are the Worlds and the Olympics.

lessons.title: Best-on-best hockey
lessons.objective: Explain why fans love these events.

statement.speaker: Casey
statement.text: Best-on-best events bring together the top players from each country.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: Each nation sends its best available players, so the matchups are elite.
options.explanation: Right. That is what best-on-best means: the stars on national teams, not just prospects or whoever is free.

options.text: Only young players compete.
options.explanation: Best-on-best rosters are full of veterans and stars of every age.

options.text: Every country must send the same number of players.
options.explanation: Each national federation picks its own roster.

payload.translation: Best-on-best tournaments give fans the top players from each country on one stage.

followUps.line: Which of those players do you enjoy most?

followUps.why: A specific best-on-best event she may have opinions on.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you forget the term, 'the real stars for each country' says the same thing.

payload.prompt: Which event was a best-on-best tournament?

options.text: The 4 Nations Face-Off.
The World Juniors.
A regular-season NHL game.
An AHL exhibition against a college team.

explanation.correct: Right. The 4 Nations Face-Off in February 2025 brought together Canada, the U.S., Sweden and Finland with their best available players. Canada won in overtime.
explanation.incorrect: The 4 Nations Face-Off was best-on-best. The Juniors is under-20, and the others do not feature national teams.

statement.speaker: Riley
statement.text: Best-on-best doesn't only mean the Olympics. The 4 Nations counted too.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: Best-on-best is a broader idea. The Olympics are one example and there are other tournaments.
options.explanation: Right. Whenever the top players play for their countries, it counts. The Olympics with NHL players and the 4 Nations are both examples.

options.text: The Olympics never have the best players.
options.explanation: The 2026 Olympics had NHL players, which made them best-on-best.

options.text: The 4 Nations was part of the Olympics.
options.explanation: It was a separate tournament, held in February 2025.

payload.translation: Best-on-best refers to any tournament with each country's top players, including the Olympics and events like the 4 Nations.

followUps.line: Do you like the Olympic version or the other tournaments more?
Do you think there should be more of them?
followUps.why: A friendly opinion question that keeps her talking.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: You do not have to list every event. One or two examples is enough.

payload.prompt: Why do fans love best-on-best tournaments?

options.text: The tickets are always cheaper.
The world's best players face each other, with national pride on the line.
The games are shorter.
Only little-known players compete.

explanation.correct: Right. Fans get the top stars from rival countries in high-stakes games, which is rare in a league season.
explanation.incorrect: The appeal is seeing the top stars from different countries play each other with national pride at stake. It has nothing to do with ticket prices or game length.

payload.prompt: Match each international event to its description.

pairs.definition: Every four years, with separate men's and women's tournaments.
An annual spring tournament for senior national teams.
A February 2025 best-on-best event with four countries.

explanation.summary: Each event has its own rhythm. The Olympics come every four years, the Worlds every spring, and best-on-best tournaments appear when the schedule allows.
explanation.sayThisLine: Which of these do you never miss?

statement.speaker: Morgan
statement.text: International hockey feels more open because the rink is wider.

options.text: Wider ice gives players more room to skate and pass.

options.text: International players are simply faster skaters.

options.text: The games are slower because the ice is bigger.

payload.translation: The wider international rink gives players more space, so the game feels more open than in the NHL.
